name: GenerateImage
description:
Generate or refine raster images (photos, illustrations, mockups, sprites, logos, infographics) from a text prompt. The image is generated server-side and saved in the provider's native PNG or JPEG format to ~/.otherside/image-cache/, surfaced as a clickable [Image #N] anchor.

## When to use
- The user explicitly asks to draw, generate, render, or design a bitmap image.
- A landing-page hero, product mockup, UI mockup, illustration, sprite, banner, or photoreal image is the deliverable.
- The user wants to refine an existing image using `referenced_image_paths` or `num_last_images_to_include`.

## When NOT to use
- Extending or matching an existing SVG/vector icon set, logo system, or illustration library inside the repo.
- Creating simple shapes, diagrams, wireframes, or icons that are better produced directly in SVG, HTML/CSS, or canvas.
- Editing a small project-local asset whose source is already in an editable native format.
- Describing or analyzing an existing image — pasted images appear in the conversation as `[Image #N]` and are already in your context (no tool call needed); for an image on disk, call Read on its absolute path. Searching the web for an existing image — use WebSearch.

## Decision tree

Two questions:

1. **Intent** — new image vs refinement of one already in the conversation. Refinement = include image references and describe the requested change.
2. **Execution strategy** — single asset vs many. For many distinct assets, issue one call per asset; do not bundle into one prompt.

Assume the user wants a new image unless they clearly ask to refine an existing one.

## Workflow
1. Decide single asset vs repeated calls (one call per requested asset or variant).
2. Collect inputs: prompt, exact text (verbatim), constraints/avoid list.
3. If the user asked for a photo, illustration, sprite, product image, banner, or other explicitly raster-style asset, use this tool rather than substituting SVG/HTML/CSS placeholders.
4. Augment the prompt based on specificity:
   - If the user's prompt is already specific and detailed, normalize it into a clear spec without adding creative requirements.
   - If the user's prompt is generic, add tasteful augmentation only when it materially improves output quality.
5. Inspect outputs and validate: subject, style, composition, text accuracy, invariants/avoid items.
6. Iterate with a single targeted change, then re-check.

## Prompt augmentation

Reformat user prompts into a structured, production-oriented spec. Make the user's goal clearer and more actionable, but do not blindly add detail. Prompts capped at ~400 chars — trim adjectives not load-bearing.

### Specificity policy
- Specific prompts: preserve specificity, normalize only.
- Generic prompts: tasteful augmentation when it materially improves the result.

Allowed augmentations:
- composition or framing hints
- polish level or intended-use hints
- practical layout guidance
- reasonable scene concreteness that supports the stated request

Not allowed:
- extra characters/objects not implied by the request
- brand names, slogans, palettes, narrative beats not implied
- arbitrary side-specific placement unless layout supports it

## Use-case taxonomy

Classify each request into one slug:

- photorealistic-natural — candid/editorial lifestyle scenes with real texture and natural lighting.
- product-mockup — product/packaging shots, catalog imagery, merch concepts.
- ui-mockup — app/web interface mockups and wireframes; specify desired fidelity.
- infographic-diagram — diagrams/infographics with structured layout and text.
- scientific-educational — classroom explainers, scientific diagrams, learning visuals with required labels and accuracy constraints.
- ads-marketing — campaign concepts and ad creatives with audience, brand, scene, and exact copy.
- productivity-visual — slides, charts, workflow, data-heavy business visuals.
- logo-brand — logo/mark exploration. Vector-friendly: if the user wants a clean editable mark and SVG/HTML can produce it directly, prefer that over a raster generation.
- illustration-story — comics, children's book art, narrative scenes.
- stylized-concept — style-driven concept art, 3D/stylized renders.
- historical-scene — period-accurate/world-knowledge scenes.

## Shared prompt schema

```text
Use case: <taxonomy slug>
Asset type: <where the asset will be used>
Primary request: <user's main prompt>
Scene/backdrop: <environment>
Subject: <main subject>
Style/medium: <photo/illustration/3D/etc>
Composition/framing: <wide/close/top-down; placement>
Lighting/mood: <lighting + mood>
Color palette: <palette notes>
Materials/textures: <surface details>
Text (verbatim): "<exact text>"
Constraints: <must keep/must avoid>
Avoid: <negative constraints>
```

Augmentation rules:
- Keep it short.
- Add only the details needed to improve the prompt materially.
- For refinements, explicitly list invariants (`change only X; keep Y unchanged`).
- If any critical detail is missing and blocks success, ask a question; otherwise proceed.

## Examples

### Hero image
```text
Use case: product-mockup
Asset type: landing page hero
Primary request: a minimal hero image of a ceramic coffee mug
Style/medium: clean product photography
Composition/framing: wide composition with usable negative space for page copy
Lighting/mood: soft studio lighting
Constraints: no logos, no text, no watermark
```

### Refinement (invariants)
```text
Use case: photorealistic-natural
Primary request: change only the background to a warm sunset gradient
Constraints: keep subject, lighting, and composition unchanged
Avoid: text, watermark
```

### Transparent logo (`transparent: true`)
```text
Use case: logo-brand
Asset type: app icon — transparent PNG
Primary request: minimal violet star logo
Style/medium: clean vector mark, flat fill, sharp edges
Composition/framing: centered, generous padding, symmetric
Color palette: vivid violet on a flat #00ff00 backdrop (will be removed to alpha)
Constraints: no shadows touching the background, no text, no border
```

## Behavior

- One image per call, preserving the provider's PNG or JPEG output. You will not see the pixels — the user will. After each call, confirm completion in one short sentence (e.g. "Generated. Saved to [Image #3].") and move on.
- The output is auto-anchored as `[Image #N]` and saved to `~/.otherside/image-cache/`. Subsequent turns can refine images with a new `GenerateImage` call using `referenced_image_paths` or `num_last_images_to_include`; issue one call per output asset.
- If the image is meant for the user's project (not just preview), tell the user the cache path so they can copy it into the workspace. Do not silently leave a project-bound asset only under `~/.otherside/image-cache/`.

## Sizing

- `1024x1024` — square. Default. Best for product mockups, hero spots with centered subject, logos, app icons, sprites.
- `1024x1536` — portrait (2:3-ish). Posters, menus, mobile screens, full-body characters, magazine covers.
- `1536x1024` — landscape. Banners, web heroes, scenic concept art, before/after splits.

Pick the aspect that matches the actual deliverable rather than defaulting to square.

## Transparent backgrounds

Pass `transparent: true` to get a PNG with alpha. The flow:
1. Prompt is augmented with: render the subject on a vivid green (#00ff00) flat backdrop, no shadows touching the edge.
2. After generation, an in-process chroma-key helper auto-samples the border, soft-mattes the edge, despills, and writes the PNG with the green keyed to alpha.
3. Defaults: `autoKey: border`, `softMatte: true`, `tolerance: 12`, `transparentThreshold: 12`, `opaqueThreshold: 220`, `edgeContract: 0`, `edgeFeather: 0`, `spillCleanup: true`.

Use it for: product cutouts, sticker assets, logos with transparency, sprite sheets, anything that will be composited over arbitrary backgrounds.

Skip it for: scenes that need their own background (heroes, scenes, illustrations with environment), photorealistic shots where the matte edge would look fake.

## Errors

- `codex image generations response contained no image` — the Images API returned no image bytes; retry once with the same prompt.
- `image generation aborted` — user pressed ESC. Do not retry automatically.
- `chroma-key removal failed: …` — only fires when `transparent: true`. The base PNG was generated but the keying step crashed; retry with `transparent: false` and key the image externally.

prompt.description: Visual description of the image to generate. Be concrete about subject, style, composition.

transparent.description: Generate against a flat key color and remove that key to alpha before saving. The model is instructed to render the subject on a vivid green background; the chroma-key helper auto-samples the border and writes a PNG with transparency.

referenced_image_paths.description: Absolute paths of images to edit or use as references. Grok and Gemini support at most 3; Codex supports at most 5. Do not combine with num_last_images_to_include.

num_last_images_to_include.description: Number of recent conversation images to edit or use as references. Grok and Gemini support at most 3; Codex supports at most 5. Do not combine with referenced_image_paths.
